minutes.headline: Voters took the Article 1 vote on a PFAS treatment plant loan; the yes count is garbled and the no count was 309.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District held a special meeting with one article, an appropriation to design and build a PFAS treatment facility at the Lancaster Avenue wellfield. It would be funded by a 0% state revolving fund loan with principal forgiveness. Most of the early meeting was ground rules and practice clicker votes. One resident asked how costs would reach water users, and was told both the minimum quarterly charge and the usage charge would rise. Electronic voting followed and the result was announced to applause, but the yes count is garbled in the captions.

public_comment.topic: Asked whether the loan and construction cost would be built into the per-100-cubic-feet water price or billed as a separate special assessment.

votes.motion: Article 1: appropriate a stated sum to design and construct a PFAS water treatment facility at the Lancaster Avenue wellfield, with borrowing authorized under G.L. c.44 and possibly the Mass. Clean Water Trust.

The district would commit to a 0% state revolving fund loan with a minimum level of principal forgiveness. The loan is described as valued at the stated amount.
The minimum quarterly charge and the tiered usage charge would both rise. The figures are averages from running rates through all meter ratings.
